10 hours ago10h ·
The winter timetable is out, and for the first time the operator has published the reasoning behind it along with the times. Every crossing is tied to a window of water deep enough for the loaded boat, and those windows move by about fifty minutes a day.
So the first and last boats are fixed to the school day and everything in between drifts with the tide. The fortnightly sheets are at both slipways and in the shop, and the skipper will still wait a minute for a running child.

Ines Varga
We moved to the island in the autumn and nobody told us the boats followed the tide rather than the clock, so the first fortnight was a series of very long waits on the slipway with the dog. Now we just ask in the shop, which is what everybody else seems to do. It would help if the sheet said somewhere near the top that the middle crossings move, because the first time you read it the times look like a mistake.

Mara Oyelaran

3h ·
Twenty years of walking the same stretch of coast every morning, and today for the first time a seal followed me the whole length of the beach, keeping pace about ten metres out and watching me the entire time.
When I stopped, it stopped. When I turned back, it turned back too. I have no idea what it wanted, but I have decided to take it as a compliment and I will be there again tomorrow at seven.
